instruction: Enumerate subdomains for target.example.com on an authorized external assessment. Provide passive-first commands and note when to escalate to active DNS.
output:
```bash
subfinder -d target.example.com -all -silent -o subs_passive.txt
amass enum -passive -d target.example.com -o subs_amass.txt
sort -u subs_passive.txt subs_amass.txt -o subs_all.txt
httpx -l subs_all.txt -title -tech-detect -status-code -o live_hosts.txt
```
Expect live hosts with 200/301/302; title/tech columns help prioritize. Stay within program scope—do not scan out-of-scope TLDs or third-party SaaS without permission.

instruction: You have a wordlist of candidate hosts for example.com. Probe which respond over HTTP/HTTPS and capture status, title, and technologies.
output:
```bash
cat hosts.txt | httpx -silent -status-code -title -tech-detect -follow-redirects -threads 50 -o httpx_results.txt
```
Filter for non-404/5xx first. Re-run with `-screenshot` only if the program allows it and storage is approved.

instruction: Run a quick nuclei scan against https://api.target.example.com for known misconfigurations and default panels. Keep rate low.
output:
```bash
nuclei -u https://api.target.example.com -severity medium,high,critical -rl 30 -c 10 -o nuclei_api.txt
```
Review findings for false positives (CDN/WAF blocks). Stop and adjust `-tags` if you trigger rate limits; document 429 responses only.

instruction: Port-scan the single host target.example.com before web testing. Use a sensible top-port scan with service detection.

```bash
nmap -sV -sC -Pn --top-ports 1000 -oA nmap_target target.example.com
```
Open 80/443/8080 are typical web entry points. Avoid aggressive `-A` on production without approval; extend ports only if scope allows full TCP.
